Outcome_metric: NO2 concentration at in-zone monitors during charging hours, 2003 to 2007 vs 2000 to 2002, relative to 20 UK control cities
Peer_reviewed_citation: Green, C. P., Heywood, J. S., & Navarro Paniagua, M. (2020). Did the London congestion charge reduce pollution? Regional Science and Urban Economics, 84, 103573.
Stringency_note: GBP 5 per day weekdays 7am to 6.30pm at launch (17 Feb 2003); GBP 8 from July 2005
Extractor_notes: DiD on hourly readings during charging hours, 2000 to 2007 (stops before Feb 2008 LEZ), treated = 2 LAQN stations inside zone (Bloomsbury, Westminster), control = monitors in 20 large UK cities; treatment-specific trends, year FE, weather controls, wild bootstrap p-values clustered by local authority. Numbers read from the accepted manuscript in the Lancaster repository (eprints.lancs.ac.uk document 107565; published version paywalled); they differ from the 2018 Lancaster working paper version, which should not be used. Table 1 col I: NO2 +7.940 (SE 1.287), wild p 0.000, on CCZ pretreatment mean 56.700 ug/m3; pct computed by extractor (7.940/56.700). Increase attributed to exempt diesel buses and taxis; authors call it the most robust result. With local authority FE (Table 3) +4.845 (about +8.5%). Synthetic control (Hull and Manchester weights) +11.026 (SE 4.650) on mean 57.186 (about +19.3%). NO (not in review pollutant list) fell -9.543 on mean 44.214 (about -21.6%). Years = midpoint of Feb 2003 to Dec 2007 post period

Outcome_metric: Traffic flow (DfT AADF) in LSOAs inside zone after 2003 vs LSOAs within 2.5 km outside the boundary
Peer_reviewed_citation: Tang, C. K., & van Ommeren, J. (2022). Accident externality of driving: Evidence from the London Congestion Charge. Journal of Economic Geography, 22(3), 547-580.
Stringency_note: GBP 5 (2003), GBP 8 (2005), GBP 10 (2011) over the pooled period; WEZ 2007 to 2010 controlled for
Extractor_notes: Abstract: the charge reduced traffic flow by 9.4% (first stage of an IV design for accidents). Journal full text not accessible; design read from the Tinbergen discussion paper TI 2020-080 version: TWFE regression of log AADF on CCZ x post with LSOA and year FE plus local controls (effectively DiD), the 9.4% matching the 2.5 km boundary sample (coef -0.0983). Full-sample coefficient in that version -0.1450 (about -13.5%). WP version also reports a non-significant placebo for LSOAs 1 km outside the boundary and no significant WEZ effect on flow (grey, not recorded). Collision panel 2000 to 2014; Years = rough midpoint of the post period, traffic years not stated

Peer_reviewed_citation: Santos, G., & Shaffer, B. (2004). Preliminary results of the London congestion charging scheme. Public Works Management & Policy, 9(2), 164-181.
Stringency_note: GBP 5 per day at launch Feb 2003
Extractor_notes: Abstract: traffic within the charging zone fell 16% and congestion about 30% in the first year; car speeds up more than 20%. Raw before-after, no control.
